message.content: I now have the full volume, revenue-per-unit, and revenue-ton-mile tables. Let me verify a couple of derived figures.

**Norfolk Southern Corp. (CIK 702165) — freight volume and revenue intensity, FY2022–FY2024**

Norfolk Southern's own operating metrics (not accounting reportable segments) show a clear pattern: **volumes recovered in 2024 after a 2023 decline, while revenue intensity (revenue per unit) fell in both years**, so revenue was roughly flat despite higher traffic.

**Freight volumes (units, thousands)**
| Commodity group | 2024 | 2023 | 2022 | 2024 vs 2023 | 2023 vs 2022 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Merchandise | 2,264.3 | 2,244.9 | 2,236.8 | +1% | —% |
| Intermodal | 4,107.7 | 3,822.4 | 3,913.1 | +7% | (2%) |
| Coal | 684.8 | 677.1 | 684.6 | +1% | (1%) |
| **Total** | **7,056.8** | **6,744.4** | **6,834.5** | **+5%** | **(1%)** |

Total units rose 4.6% in 2024 (calculated from the disclosed totals) after a 1.3% dip in 2023. Intermodal drove the 2024 recovery: domestic units +5% (2,500.0k vs 2,371.6k) and international +11% (1,607.7k vs 1,450.8k), the latter helped by demand, existing-customer growth and more empty-container moves. Coal tonnage was essentially flat (76.7M tons in 2024 vs 75.9M in 2023), with utility tonnage down 3% and export up 20% in 2023. On a longer measure, revenue ton miles were 178bn (2024), 176bn (2023) and 179bn (2022).

**Revenue intensity (average revenue per unit, $/unit)**
| Group | 2024 | 2023 | 2022 | 2024 vs 2023 | 2023 vs 2022 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Merchandise | 3,299 | 3,275 | 3,277 | +1% | —% |
| Intermodal | 740 | 808 | 941 | (8%) | (14%) |
| Coal | 2,352 | 2,530 | 2,532 | (7%) | —% |
| **Total** | **1,718** | **1,802** | **1,865** | **(5%)** | **(3%)** |

Revenue per thousand revenue ton miles followed the same path: $68.09 (2024), $69.05 (2023), $71.35 (2022). Management attributes the decline to lower fuel surcharge revenue (fuel surcharge revenues fell to $962M in 2024 from $1.2bn in 2023 and $1.6bn in 2022), adverse mix, lower intermodal storage revenue, and — in 2024 — decreased pricing in intermodal.

**Net effect on revenue:** total railway operating revenues were $12,123M (2024), $12,156M (2023) and $12,745M (2022) — down 0.3% in 2024 (calculated) and 4.6% in 2023. The 2024 volume gains ($314M of volume-driven revenue across the three groups) were more than offset by fuel surcharge declines and rate/mix effects.

**Summary:** volume trend turned positive in 2024 (+5%) after a soft 2023, but revenue intensity weakened for a second consecutive year (−5% in 2024, −3% in 2023), concentrated in intermodal and coal; merchandise pricing held roughly flat. Management guides 2025 revenue to increase on higher volumes.

Sources: Norfolk Southern 2024 Form 10-K (report_end 2024-12-31), Item 1 five-year statistics table (chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:9600) and MD&A revenue/units/revenue-per-unit tables (chunks :94400, :96000, :97600); 2023 Form 10-K (report_end 2023-12-31) for intermodal units and coal tonnage (chunks :91200, :92800). Percent changes for total units and total revenue are my calculations from disclosed totals; all other percentages are as disclosed.
